case_title: SHEO SHANKAR SINGH v. STATE OF JHARKHAND & ANR.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; Arms Act s.27
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Confirmed conviction and enhanced sentence to death
neutral_facts: The accused were involved in a conflict with the victim, who was a sitting member of the State Legislative Assembly. The victim opposed the accused's activities, which led to the accused killing him. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts and circumstantial evidence, including the seizure of a motorcycle and blood-stained clothing. The victim was riding a motorcycle with an eyewitness when he was shot by the accused. Medical evidence supported the eyewitness account, showing the victim sustained fatal gunshot injuries. The trial court convicted the accused of murder and sentenced them to life imprisonment, while the High Court enhanced the sentence to death. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction but commuted the death sentence to life imprisonment, finding the case did not meet the 'rarest of rare' criteria for the death penalty.
